subtitle: Dolphin
_subtitle_source: subtitle names the backend the player will actually run, the same way 18 manifests say "BizHawk".
_platform_source: the world's own setup guide requires "[Dolphin Gamecube/Wii Emulator]" and "Your US ISO file, probably named `Custom Robo (USA).iso`" -- a GameCube disc image.
_drafted_note: Drafted 2026-08-25 from the world's OWN repository -- its __init__.py, archipelago.json, setup guide and README, read that day. No field is filled in from memory or from what other games on the same console do.
_ap_world_name_source: the world's own archipelago.json: {"game": "Custom Robo"}, read 25 Aug 2026.
description: Custom Robo as a multiworld. Robo parts and the progressive Rahu evolution are shuffled; every battle and every first use of a part is a check. Requires the player's own US disc, Dolphin with MMU disabled, and the world's gclib folder installed into Archipelago's lib directory.
_description_source: written by us from the world's own structure and its setup guide's stated requirements. No text is copied from the game.
_checks_verified_note: FALSE. Nobody has played this. For a kind=world game the checks travel through the WORLD'S client, not through London -- so what is unproven here is not a RAM map of ours (there is none) but the whole chain: apworld installs, emulator starts over the bridge, the world's client attaches and carries a check. London warns at launch while this is false, which is exactly right until a tester reports one.
_requires_source: GameCube title. The setup guide lists it among the player's own requirements: "Your US ISO file, probably named `Custom Robo (USA).iso`".

rom.description: Your own Custom Robo disc image for GameCube -- the US release, as an .iso file (the world's client will not accept other container formats)
rom._description_source: the setup guide: "Your US ISO file, probably named `Custom Robo (USA).iso`". The .iso-only restriction is the guide's own troubleshooting note: "please double check your rom that is a .iso ONLY! You cannot convert into .iso from other file formats."
rom._hash_note: No hash is claimed. The guide states none.

emulator.name: Dolphin
emulator._source: the setup guide says to install Dolphin "making sure to install the most recent version" -- a direction, not a version number, so no minimum is recorded. The guide DOES state a hard setting: "Make sure Dolphin's MMU (Memory Management Unit) is disabled", which is carried in the description because nothing else reaches the player.

client.name: Custom Robo Client
client._name_source: the world registers it under this exact display name in worlds/custom_robo/__init__.py: `Component(display_name="Custom Robo Client", ..., component_type=Type.CLIENT)`. The launcher subprocess is named "CustomRoboClient"; the display name is what the player sees in the list.
client._kind_source: the world ships and registers its OWN Archipelago client: worlds/custom_robo/__init__.py does `Component(display_name="Custom Robo Client", ..., component_type=Type.CLIENT)` and launches it with `launch_subprocess(sync_main, name="CustomRoboClient")`. The transport is the world's own: CRClient.py imports dolphin_memory_engine and talks to Dolphin directly. London must NOT read memory for this game.
client._protocol_source: extensions/dolphin/extension.json declares {"protocol": "dolphin"} and DolphinBridge.Systems are ["GC", "Wii", "WII"]. The world reaches Dolphin itself through dolphin_memory_engine, which is the same emulator our bridge starts.
client._lua_note: No Lua. dolphin_memory_engine attaches to the running emulator process; there is no connector script to load.

apworld._source: the author's own releases page; the newest release read 25 Aug 2026 is V0.3, carrying custom_robo.apworld, lib-windows.zip, lib-linux.zip and a sample YAML. ⚠ The apworld is NOT enough on its own -- see _manual_setup_note.
apworld._world_version_source: the world's archipelago.json: {"world_version": "0.1.1"}. ⚠ The newest release tag reads V0.3, so the world's own file and its tag disagree. Recorded as the world states it, with the difference visible.
apworld._minimum_ap_version_source: the world's archipelago.json: {"minimum_ap_version": "0.6.3"}. Our client is 0.6.7, so this is satisfied.

_patch_extension_source: read from the world's own source, 25 Aug 2026: the 11 .py files in worlds/custom_robo were searched. cr_rom.py defines an APPatch-family class with a patch_file_ending, and CRPatcher.py a result_file_ending, but NO `APPatchExtension` appears -- so there are no custom Python patch steps for London's patcher to refuse.
_patch_note: There is deliberately NO `patch` block. This world DOES produce a patch (a `.apcr` file), but for a kind=world game Archipelago's own "Open Patch" applies it and then starts the world's client -- the setup guide says so: "This action will AUTOMATICALLY run the Custom Robo Client." London neither builds nor applies it.

_manual_setup_note: ⚠ THIS GAME NEEDS A SETUP STEP LONDON CANNOT DO. The setup guide requires the player to download lib-windows.zip (or lib-linux.zip) from the same release and extract its `gclib` folder into their Archipelago installation's /lib directory. Without it the world's client cannot reach Dolphin. London installs the apworld and starts the emulator; the gclib step and the MMU setting are the player's, and are named in `description` because that is the field that reaches them.
